findings.claim: The camel humps are still seated on the pre-wave-7 back — seat() computes the back point from topY(u) and a raw cx-bodyW+2*bodyW*u x-mapping, while the drawn back is the dorsal() envelope on the inset axA/axB axis; the identical drift was diagnosed and fixed for the tail but the humps never received the fix.
findings.evidence: seat() lines 866-869: `hx = cx - bodyW + 2 * bodyW * u; return [hx, topY(u) + bodyH * 0.06]`. The torso's actual back is the Tube envelope of dorsal() (lines 449-453, topY minus croup/withers lifts) on the inset axis axA/axB (lines 457-458, inset by 0.8*RAD from cx-bodyW/cx+bodyW). Two formulas for "the point on the back at u" that agreed before wave 7 and no longer do (~0.8*RAD(0) horizontal offset at the ends, plus the lift terms vertically). The tail comment at lines 1496-1502 names this exact failure mode ("THE TAIL WAS STILL ANCHORED TO THE PRE-WAVE-7 BODY") and its fix moved the tail onto AX/RAD; seat() still uses the old anchors, so any future edit to dorsal()/AX moves the back but not the humps.
findings.speciesHit: Camel, Bactrian Camel, Dromedary Camel (the only humps writers, quadrupedoverrides.ts:1747-1749)

findings.claim: The humpback flipper's 'scalloped leading edge' stroke recomputes the leading-edge curve with a symmetric sine formula that has drifted from the asymmetric bezier used for the fill, so the knobbed edge line floats off the wing — ending ~0.32H (~12px) above the actual wingtip instead of on it.
findings.evidence: Fill leading edge (lines 316-317): moveTo(0,-H*0.34) then bezierCurveTo(L*0.42*k,-H*0.72, L*0.86*k,-H*0.58, L*1.00*k,-H*0.02) — ends at y=-0.02H. Stroke (lines 325-328): y = -H*(0.34+Math.sin(u*PI)*0.38)+Math.sin(u*26)*2.4 over the same x span (x=u*L*k) — symmetric, returning to y=-0.34H at u=1. They agree only at the root (u=0, both -0.34H); at u=0.5 the stroke sits ~0.17H above the fill edge and at the tip 0.32H above it. The comment at 321-322 says this stroke IS the leading edge ('that bumpy edge is the one detail that separates it from every other whale'). Applies to both calls: far flipper (line 333) and near flipper (line 381).

Line 722 adds fin height only when t >= 0.45: '(t < 0.45 ? 0 : S*0.030*Math.sin((t-0.45)/0.55*Math.PI))'. Line 749-750 places the oral disc/head at at(1) ('const [hx, hy] = at(1)'), and line 740 places the gill pores 'behind the head' at t=0.632..0.80 — confirming t=1 is the head end and t=0 the tail end. findings.claim: The cloak-squid web outline anchors its start at the LEFT shoulder but the first arm tip in the sweep is the RIGHTMOST arm (and its final segment runs leftmost tip to RIGHT shoulder), so the first and last web 'scallops' are two full-width chords that cross each other instead of joining adjacent structures; nonzero-winding fill hides the crossing inside the shape, but beyond each shoulder the cape's upper boundary is a chord attached to the opposite-side shoulder.
findings.evidence: Line 1705: c.moveTo(cx - mw*0.9, ...) starts at the left shoulder. Line 1696: a = Math.PI*(0.16 + t*0.68), so armTip[0] has cos(0.16*PI)=+0.876 — the far RIGHT side (tips reach x = cx ± ~2.2mw, well outside the ±0.9mw shoulders) — and armTip[7] is far left. Line 1708 pairs prev=[cx - mw*0.9, ...] with armTip[0] for the first quadratic (a left-shoulder-to-right-tip chord), and line 1711 runs lineTo(cx + mw*0.9, ...) from armTip[7] on the left (a left-tip-to-right-shoulder chord). Swapping the moveTo and the closing lineTo x-signs (or reversing the arm order) would make the scallops adjacent as the comment at 1691-1692 intends ('one continuous web joining all eight arms').
findings.speciesHit: Vampire Squid, Deep-Sea Octopus

findings.evidence: artaudit.mjs:56 requires the line to match /^\s*void r;\s*$/ and artaudit.mjs:67 requires the enclosing assignment to match /const r = (nrng|rngF|mulberry32)\(/. But floraoverrides3.ts, faunaoverrides4.ts and fungioverrides2.ts seed exclusively via `const r = seeded(g, 0x...)` (e.g. floraoverrides3.ts:60,105,199,224; faunaoverrides4.ts:212; fungioverrides2.ts:232,281) and carry untagged discards at floraoverrides3.ts:100,194,219,261, faunaoverrides4.ts:255, fungioverrides2.ts:266,302 — grep confirms zero '@rng-unused' tags in any of those files. faunaoverrides5.ts:1123 (`void r; void near;`, seeded via nrng at 1120-area) dodges the line-shape test instead. The gate's clean summary (artaudit.mjs:138) is therefore asserted over painters it never examined — defect class B shipping unflagged under the very instrument built for it.
findings.speciesHit: painters in floraoverrides3, faunaoverrides4, fungioverrides2, faunaoverrides5 whose per-species randomness does nothing

findings.claim: --update disables the D-ART-100 capability guard for EVERY name in the batch, not just previously-hued rows, letting an update run insert a brand-new `hue:` into a painter that never reads hue — via a fallback regex that matches any call's first brace.
findings.evidence: Line 51 `if (!update && !capable.has(name))` skips the fixable-list check wholesale when --update is set (the flag's own comment, line 32 and 81-82, scopes it to 're-tune hex hues this pass set'). For a never-hued name the apply loop then passes line 83's `/\bhue:/` test as false, reaches line 89 where `capable.get(key)` is undefined, and line 91's alternation `'\b' + painter + '\s*\(|\b\w+\s*\(\s*\{'` still matches ANY `fn({` (or indexOf('{',0) picks the first brace on the line when the regex misses), so line 96 writes `hue: '#...'` into an arbitrary spec object — the inert-field insertion the header (lines 7-11) says this tool exists to refuse.
findings.speciesHit: any species passed in an --update batch that was never hued by this pass

findings.claim: The string-array route-list matcher only sees a single-quoted FIRST entry per line — the double-quote fix applied to the object-key matcher eight lines above never reached it — so six of FLORA_DUPES' seven names (including double-quoted "Devil's Club") are invisible and classed verbatim-flora.
findings.evidence: artclass.mjs:67 `/^ {2}'([^']+)',/gm` is single-quote-only and line-anchored, while line 59's object matcher was explicitly fixed to read both quotings (comment lines 52-58: 'when a key can be written two ways, read both'). floraoverrides.ts:259 packs the whole FLORA_DUPES array on one line: `'Acai', 'Salmonberry', 'Licorice', "Devil's Club", 'Green Algae', 'Ice Algae', 'Snow Algae', ];` — only 'Acai' is captured; the rest fall through classOf to 'verbatim-flora', the class artclass's header says 'must NEVER move'.
findings.speciesHit: Salmonberry, Licorice, Devil's Club, Green Algae, Ice Algae, Snow Algae

findings.claim: Check H's 'buildsAlways' detector matches any line-starting execSync regardless of an enclosing if-block, so a conditional rebuild formatted as a block-if is classified as an unconditional build and check H can never fire on it.
findings.evidence: artaudit.mjs:125 `buildsAlways = /^\s*execSync\('npx vite build'/m.test(t)` — a purely lexical line test. speciesstrip.mjs:50-52 is `if (!built || ...mtimeMs < srcMs) {\n      execSync('npx vite build', ...)` — a conditional build whose execSync begins a line, so it tests true as 'always'. The buildsMaybe pattern (line 126) only recognizes the single-line `if (!fs.existsSync(...)) execSync(...)` form. Any future tool that guards its build with a block-if (even `if (false) { execSync('npx vite build') }`) passes H while reading a stale bundle — the D-ART-36 detector passes for the wrong reason.

findings.claim: The freshness proof measures only packages/art/src mtimes, but the vite build compiles apps/game source too — an edit to the audit harness leaves dist/audit.html classified fresh and the strip renders through yesterday's harness.
findings.evidence: speciesstrip.mjs:47 `const srcMs = newest(path.join(here, '..', 'packages', 'art', 'src'))` is the sole input to the rebuild decision at line 50, while the artifact it gates (dist/audit.html) is built from appDir = apps/game (lines 15, 51). Changes under apps/game/src (the audit page that defines __CF_STRIP__ and the genome plumbing the header says makes 'what a human judges exactly what the audit measured') never advance srcMs, so the stale-bundle skip fires on a bundle that is not fresh with respect to all of its inputs.

findings.claim: All three owls set `bill: 'hook'` but the entire bill-drawing block runs only when `!opts.owl` — for these setters the field is read in a branch they can never reach, and the owl branch draws its own fixed triangle beak instead.
findings.evidence: Writers: birdoverrides.ts:32-34 ('Owl', 'Snowy Owl', 'Desert Owl' all pass bill:'hook'). Reader: faunaoverrides.ts:930 `if (!opts.owl) {` guards every `opts.bill` read (lines 956-996); the owl path draws a hardcoded #e0b13c triangle at faunaoverrides.ts:915-916. `bill` is a required BirdSpec field (faunaoverrides.ts:508) so the rows are forced to write a value that cannot change the drawing — the nosePad shape: read-but-not-for-its-setters.
findings.speciesHit: Owl, Snowy Owl, Desert Owl

findings.claim: The crop comment claims 'Drawn before the head so the neck sits on top of it', but the crop is filled AFTER the neck is stroked, so the crop paints over the neck — the neck cannot sit on top of it. (Found tracing birdoverrides' painter; file itself is outside this bundle.)

The comment at 876-877 asserts the opposite layering for the neck (only the head, drawn at 893, lands on top). Same D-ART-137 shape as the shipped 'drawn behind the head' incident.

findings.claim: The morphology-pass cache-key fix (fold _earthName into the key so a corrected species caches distinctly from its fallback) was applied to speciesPortrait's key but not to speciesThumb's copied key formula, so the thumb cache still collides corrected and fallback genomes.
findings.evidence: Writer/reader trace: speciesart.ts:19 key = seed+'_'+(gen||0)+'_'+kingdom+apex+par+ '_'+nm, with lines 16-17 stating the purpose ('the key folds in _earthName so a corrected species caches distinctly from its fallback'). speciesart.ts:32 computes the identical formula WITHOUT nm. speciesThumb serves real UI from mixed genome populations: main.ts:280 (Compendium rows over saved genomes — Earth-captured entries carry _earthName via _earthNamePass, main.ts:1539/apphooks.ts:85; non-Earth entries do not) and main.ts:1639 (planetside). Two genomes agreeing on seed/gen/kingdom/apex/par but differing in _earthName get ONE thumb slot: first render pins its 132px art for the other. The collision is also sticky: speciesart.ts:13 pagehide flush clears only speciesArtCache, never speciesThumbCache. In main.js (lines 2262/2287) neither key had the fold; the v2 port fixed one of the two parallel caches and left the sibling on the pre-fix formula — the same shape as the v1.8.6 size-clamp incident.
findings.speciesHit: Every species routed by resolveOverride (the OVERRIDE_COUNT set + CANON + procedural path) whose remaining key tuple can also occur on an un-named or differently-named genome; blast is the 132px thumb shown in Compendium rows and the planetside strip, not the full portrait.

findings.claim: Header claims 'bodies verbatim from main.js 2249-2308', but the speciesPortrait body is not verbatim: it inserts the resolveOverride() consult and changes the cache-key formula, both v2-only.
findings.evidence: speciesart.ts:1-4 asserts 'bodies verbatim from main.js 2249-2308'. main.js:2262 key has no nm component and main.js:2267-2269 dispatches straight to the four hdPortrait* painters; speciesart.ts:19 adds the '_'+nm fold and speciesart.ts:21 adds resolveOverride(g) ?? before the painter chain. The deviation is intended and documented two lines later (lines 16-17, 'THE MORPHOLOGY PASS'), which makes the header's 'verbatim' claim internally contradicted — a parity pass that trusts the header and diffs against main.js could 'restore' the override consult away.

findings.claim: Unreachable duplicate guard: 'if (!name) return null;' directly follows 'if (!name) return resolveProcedural(g);', so the null return can never execute — a stale pre-wave-13 fall-through left in place. (Outside bundle 16; found while tracing the bundle's direct callee.)
findings.evidence: speciesoverrides.ts:524 'if (!name) return resolveProcedural(g);' returns for every falsy name; speciesoverrides.ts:525 'if (!name) return null;' tests the identical condition and is dead. The wave-13 comment (lines 519-523) describes replacing the fall-through with the procedural path; the old return was kept instead of deleted. Dormant-row hazard: any edit that removes or reorders line 524 silently makes 'return null' the live behavior for every bred/procedural genome, reverting twelve waves of procedural art routing.
